name: ultimate-file-manager-pro
readme_summary: Ultimate File Manager Pro is a high-performance, dual-pane file manager for Android Mobile, Android TV, and Windows PC. It focuses on privacy, efficiency, and speed, enabling seamless side-by-side file operations, LAN discovery, remote PC pairing, and multi-protocol network storage access.
key_features: Dual-pane file management
Support for Android Mobile, Android TV/Fire TV, and Windows PC
LAN auto-discovery
Remote PC pairing
Multi-protocol network storage access
Privacy-focused and efficient design
primary_use_case: Managing files efficiently across multiple platforms (Android mobile, Android TV, Windows PC) using a dual-pane interface, with advanced features for network and remote access.
cover_image_prompt: A wise, old librarian standing at a grand, ornate desk with two large, open books side-by-side. One book displays a chaotic jumble of papers and files, while the other shows them neatly organized and categorized. The librarian is using a magical quill to transfer items from the messy book to the organized one. Subtle glowing lines connect the two books, representing data transfer. In the background, a faint map shows connections to different devices like a smartphone, a TV, and a PC. The scene is set in a warm, cozy library with soft lighting. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear iconography and a clean composition, featuring the 'Ultimate File Manager Pro' logo subtly placed on the desk.

name: cursor-smith
readme_summary: Cursor-Smith is a highly customizable cursor engine for Obsidian, allowing users to personalize their text caret with various styles, colors, and animations. It offers a wide array of effects and options to enhance the writing experience for users who desire a more visually engaging or functional cursor.
key_features: Extensive cursor styling (box, line, underline, solid, hollow, gradients, thickness, opacity, glow)
Customizable blinking animations (speed, balance, fade, breathing)
Smooth cursor gliding animation with speed-based responsiveness
Support for multiple cursors with identical styling
Eleven distinct visual effects (pop, typewriter, pixel trail, stardust, bracket tether, motion smear, energy beam, CRT, speed demon, hot-head, torch spotlight)
Stackable effects with individual settings
Respects reduced motion settings
Easy installation via Obsidian Community Plugins
primary_use_case: To provide users of Obsidian with advanced and highly customizable text cursor styles and animations, enhancing the visual appeal and user experience of the writing environment.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, magical blacksmith forging a glowing, animated cursor in a cozy, dimly lit workshop. The blacksmith, representing Cursor-Smith, hammers sparks of light onto an anvil shaped like an Obsidian logo. The sparks transform into various cursor styles – a solid box, a shimmering underline, a pulsing line – that float upwards. In the background, a stylized Obsidian interface is visible, with the newly forged cursors elegantly guiding text. The overall mood is creative and inspiring, with a focus on the transformation of a simple cursor into a personalized work of art. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with warm, inviting lighting and rich textures.

name: google-play-scraper
description: Google Play scraper for Node.js with a fully typed TypeScript API. App details, search, top charts, reviews, permissions and data safety. A modern replacement for the unmaintained google-play-scraper.
readme_summary: This Node.js library provides a fully typed TypeScript API to scrape data from the Google Play Store. It allows developers to fetch app details, search results, reviews, and more, serving as a modern, robust alternative to older scrapers.
key_features: Scrape app details, search results, top charts, developer pages, similar apps, user reviews, permissions, and data safety.
Fully typed results with runtime validation using Zod schemas.
Runs on native Node.js fetch (no external HTTP dependency).
Resilient design with fallback paths for fragile data structures.
Daily contract tests against Google Play to detect layout changes.
Typed error classes for better error handling.
Includes throttling, retries, and caching.
Supports both ESM and CommonJS module formats.
primary_use_case: Scraping Google Play Store data for market research, ASO, competitor tracking, and review monitoring.
cover_image_prompt: A diligent librarian meticulously organizing and cataloging an immense, overflowing library of digital books representing Android apps. The librarian uses a magnifying glass that highlights specific app details like ratings and download counts, transforming raw data streams into neatly arranged shelves. Small, glowing data particles flow from a 'Google Play' portal into the library. The repository name 'google-play-scraper' is subtly etched on a nearby desk. The scene is set in a clean, modern library with soft, ambient lighting. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style with clear iconography and a focus on organized data flow.

name: tui-use
description: tui-use lets agents interact with programs that expect a human at the keyboard — REPLs, debuggers, TUI apps, and anything else bash can't reach.
readme_summary: tui-use enables AI agents to interact with terminal-based programs like REPLs, debuggers, and TUI applications, which are typically inaccessible to automated scripts. It provides a way to send keystrokes and read the screen output as plain text, bridging the gap between human-interactive programs and AI agents.
key_features: Full VT Rendering: Processes PTY output accurately, including ANSI escape sequences, for clean plain text screen content.
Smart Wait: Debounces screen updates to detect stability and can wait for specific text patterns, eliminating guesswork for AI agents.
Snapshot Model: Provides explicit screen states and interactions (read, decide, type) without complex async stream management.
Highlights: Identifies inverse-video spans (selected items) on screen, allowing agents to understand UI focus.
primary_use_case: Allowing AI agents to interact with and control terminal-based applications (REPLs, debuggers, TUI apps) that require human input.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled puppeteer, represented by a stylized AI robot hand, is expertly manipulating a complex network of glowing digital strings. These strings connect to various miniature, interactive terminal windows displaying code, debuggers, and TUI applications like vim and htop. The robot hand is shown precisely sending keystrokes (visualized as small data packets) into the terminals and receiving clear, text-based screen updates (visualized as flowing information streams) in return. The scene is set against a dark, futuristic backdrop with subtle code snippets and data visualizations integrated into the environment, emphasizing the control and interaction. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a vibrant, technological color palette, clearly conveying the concept of an AI agent controlling terminal programs.

name: musicat
description: A sleek desktop music player and tagger for offline music 🪕. With gapless playback, smart playlists, and a map view! Built with Svelte and Tauri
readme_summary: Musicat is a sleek, cross-platform desktop music player and tagger built with Svelte and Tauri, designed for managing local music libraries. It offers features like gapless playback, smart playlists, metadata editing, album art fetching, lyrics retrieval, and unique visualizations like waveform and map views.
key_features: Supports MP3, FLAC, WAV, AAC, OGG
Linked library using original files
Gapless playback (same sample rate)
Metadata tagger (ID3v2, Vorbis)
Auto-watch and re-scan folders
Smart playlists
Download album art and origin country
Fetch lyrics
World Map view of library
Waveform view
Stats and album timeline
primary_use_case: Managing and enhancing a local music library with a modern, feature-rich desktop application.
cover_image_prompt: A digital librarian, depicted as a friendly robot with glowing data streams, meticulously organizing a vast, colorful library of vinyl records and digital music files. The robot is placing records onto shelves that morph into a world map, with glowing pins indicating the origin of each album. Small, translucent screens float around, displaying waveform visualizations and song lyrics. The overall scene is clean, modern, and slightly whimsical, with a focus on the joy of rediscovering and connecting with music. The style should be a vibrant 3D isometric illustration with soft, ambient lighting, emphasizing the 'Musicat' name subtly etched on the robot's chassis.
